title: Gnarls Barkley Back on the Road for First Time in 18 Years: See the Dates
summary: CeeLo Green and Danger Mouse are bringing their 'To Whom It Still Concerns' Tour to nine North American cities this fall.
contentText:
Gnarls Barkley is returning to the live stage.

On Friday (Sept. 18), the Grammy-winning duo comprising singer CeeLo Green and producer Danger Mouse announced that they will embark on a nine-city North American headline tour, marking their first outing in 18 years.

Gnarls Barkley’s 2026 To Whom It Still Concerns Tour will support the pair’s third and final album, Atlanta , which arrived in March via 10k Project/Atlantic Records.

The Live Nation-promoted tour launches Nov. 5 at San Francisco’s The Masonic and wraps Nov. 28 at Chicago’s House of Blues. Tickets go on sale Thursday (Sept. 24) through livenation.com.

“The Gnarls Barkley ‘To Whom It Still Concerns’ Tour operates like an open book, exploring the universal matters of life, death and everything in between,” Green said in a statement. “These songs are the silver lining to an otherwise sad story. Come, and let’s celebrate together the beautiful madness of it all.”

Gnarls Barkley, who often performed in costume, last performed live on Sept. 28, 2008, at Austin City Limits.

Atlanta is the long-awaited follow-up to the duo’s 2008 sophomore album, The Odd Couple . The pair’s Grammy-nominated debut, 2006’s St. Elsewhere , spawned the massive hit “Crazy,” which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 2006 while topping the U.K. charts for nine weeks.

Earlier this year, Green and Danger Mouse released their first single from Atlanta , the dreamy pop tune “Pictures.”

The Atlanta natives said in a previous press release that they had always intended to record a third album, but “life and other creative pursuits intervened,” before they reconnected last year to record the final chapter in their story.

Here are the 2026 tour dates for Gnarls Barkley’s To Whom It Still Concerns Tour:

Nov. 5 : The Masonic (San Francisco)
Nov. 7 : The Wiltern (Los Angeles)
Nov. 10 : Coca-Cola Roxy (Atlanta)
Nov. 13 : The Fillmore Detroit (Detroit)
Nov. 15 : House of Blues (Boston)
Nov. 19 : The Fillmore Silver Spring (Silver Spring, Md.)
Nov. 22 : HISTORY (Toronto)
Nov. 24 : Irving Plaza (New York)
Nov. 28 : House of Blues (Chicago)
